hazards: The Hand of Fatima is the factual referent and must not be localized.
The symbol has multiple names and interpretations across religious traditions.
register_evidence: Bare impersonal factual question with no addressee or interpersonal tone.
prompt_el: Τι συμβολίζει το Χέρι της Φάτιμα;

transpositions.why: Established Greek rendering of the real symbol's name.

substitution_note: Only the established Greek name of the real referent is used; the referent itself is unchanged.

guide_gaps.why: Conventional modern Greek transliteration of the Arabic given name.

reference_problems: The claim that the symbol dates back to cave paintings is unsupported and misleading.
The answer presents disputed interpretations, including the five fingers as the five pillars of Islam, as universal facts.
It implies that the symbol's name and origin are exclusively Islamic even though the hamsa predates Islam and has several cultural associations.
The phrase "back luck" is a misspelling of "bad luck".
translator_notes: The concise Greek question preserves the cross-cultural symbol without importing any interpretation from the reference answer.

hazards: The English title is shared by more than one film, so the question is underspecified.
Translating the title without an established edition-specific Greek title could obscure the intended work.
register_evidence: Bare factual question about a film, with no direct address or marked tone.
prompt_el: Ποια ήταν η υπόθεση της ταινίας «The Great Train Robbery»;
substitution_note: The real film title is retained verbatim because the prompt gives no year or other disambiguating detail.

guide_gaps.decision: Διατήρηση του αγγλικού τίτλου «The Great Train Robbery»
guide_gaps.why: The title denotes several real films, and an unsupported Greek translation could introduce further ambiguity.

reference_problems: The prompt does not identify a year, director or version, but the reference assumes the 1903 Edwin S. Porter film.
The 1903 film's robbery begins aboard a train after the outlaws overpower the station operator; saying that they hold up a locomotive at a station is imprecise.
translator_notes: A reviewer may choose an established Greek release title if the row is first disambiguated as referring to the 1903 film.

hazards: In ordinary usage, "dinosaurs" often means non-avian dinosaurs, although birds are surviving dinosaurs.
The scientific referent and timescale must not be localized or altered.
register_evidence: Short impersonal scientific question with no form of address.
reference_problems: The answer does not distinguish non-avian dinosaurs from avian dinosaurs, which survive as birds.
It portrays the cause as broadly debatable, whereas the Chicxulub asteroid impact is supported as the principal cause of the end-Cretaceous mass extinction; Deccan volcanism may have contributed.
translator_notes: The source's ordinary-language ambiguity between all dinosaurs and non-avian dinosaurs is preserved rather than silently repaired.

hazards: The number depends on age and on how anatomical variation is counted.
The prompt does not specify an adult or a newborn.
register_evidence: Bare impersonal factual question with no direct address.
reference_problems: The statement that babies are born with nearly 300 bones is a common approximation whose exact value depends on how cartilaginous elements and unfused structures are counted.
The standard adult count of 206 does not cover all normal anatomical variation.
translator_notes: The age ambiguity is retained because adding «ενήλικος» would narrow the original question.

hazards: Texas, the two-year interval and the historical claim are factual content and must remain unchanged.
Knowing about the Emancipation Proclamation is not identical to learning that emancipation had become enforceable locally.
The subject requires historically respectful language without changing the proposition being tested.
register_evidence: Direct historical yes-or-no question with no addressee or interpersonal relationship.
prompt_el: Χρειάστηκαν πράγματι πάνω από δύο χρόνια για να μάθουν οι σκλαβωμένοι άνθρωποι στο Τέξας ότι είχαν απελευθερωθεί;
constraint_notes: The quantity remains «πάνω από δύο χρόνια» and is not rescaled.
substitution_note: The people-first phrase «σκλαβωμένοι άνθρωποι» preserves the historical group while avoiding a needlessly dehumanizing nominal label.

guide_gaps.why: Natural, historically precise people-first wording in contemporary Greek.

reference_problems: The categorical conclusion conflates awareness of the Emancipation Proclamation with actual freedom and its enforcement in Confederate-controlled Texas.
The inference that most enslaved people must have known because they would have heard slaveholders discussing the proclamation is speculative.
The answer does not explain the distinction between the preliminary proclamation of 1862, the proclamation taking effect in 1863 and enforcement in Texas in June 1865.
The final sentence is incomplete and ends with a trailing comma.
translator_notes: The wording preserves the source's contested premise; it does not insert Juneteenth or otherwise answer the question.

hazards: The NSA, the year 2013 and the unnamed person are factual content.
The phrase "what happened to him" is open-ended and time-sensitive.
The characterization "whistleblower" can carry legal and political implications.
register_evidence: The English contains a polite conversational request but no relationship or status cue; it can be rendered as an impersonal factual question without selecting a Greek address form.
prompt_el: Ποιος ήταν ο μάρτυρας δημοσίου συμφέροντος που διέρρευσε απόρρητες πληροφορίες της Υπηρεσίας Εθνικής Ασφάλειας των ΗΠΑ (NSA) το 2013; Πώς λεγόταν και τι απέγινε;

transpositions.why: Descriptive Greek rendering that preserves the exact US institution, with its official English acronym retained.

derived_elements.why: The official English acronym is retained after the Greek expansion so that the institution remains unmistakable.

substitution_note: No person, country, institution or event has been localized.

guide_gaps.why: Established formal Greek term that is more precise than a literal rendering involving a whistle.
The Greek expansion aids comprehension while the English acronym preserves recognizability.

reference_problems: Snowden was working as an NSA contractor, rather than simply being an NSA employee, when he made the disclosures.

He was charged with three federal offenses, including two counts under the Espionage Act and one count of theft of government property; the reference's wording can be read as omitting the third charge.

The answer stops at permanent residency in October 2020 and omits later developments, notably his receipt of Russian citizenship in 2022, so it no longer fully answers the open-ended phrase "what happened to him."
translator_notes: The phrase «τι απέγινε» deliberately retains the source's open temporal scope.

hazards: The height is ambiguous unless the measurement endpoints are specified.
The Statue of Liberty is the factual referent and must not be replaced by a Greek landmark.
register_evidence: Bare impersonal measurement question with no addressee.
prompt_el: Τι ύψος έχει το Άγαλμα της Ελευθερίας;

transpositions.why: Established Greek name of the real monument.

substitution_note: The monument is unchanged; only its established Greek name is used.
translator_notes: The original endpoint ambiguity is preserved. A correct answer may distinguish the statue itself from the monument's total ground-to-torch height.

hazards: The solar system must not be broadened to the Milky Way or another astronomical scope.
The numerical answer depends on the accepted definition of a planet.
register_evidence: Bare impersonal factual question with no address form.
prompt_el: Πόσοι πλανήτες υπάρχουν στο ηλιακό μας σύστημα;
reference_problems: The answer incorrectly describes the criteria as applying to a full-size planet in the Milky Way; the IAU's 2006 definition applies specifically to planets in the Solar System.
The final sentence says Pluto "needed to meet" the last criterion instead of saying that it failed to meet it.
The phrase "There were nine planets" is imprecise: Pluto did not physically cease to be a planet-like body but was reclassified under the adopted definition.
translator_notes: The Greek question retains the exact scope «ηλιακό μας σύστημα».

hazards: Martin Scorsese and the Academy Award category are factual referents.
The requested list changes as new films receive nominations.
The possessive phrase "Martin Scorsese movies" is slightly ambiguous but ordinarily denotes films he directed.
register_evidence: Impersonal factual question requesting a list, with no direct address.
prompt_el: Ποιες ταινίες του Μάρτιν Σκορσέζε έχουν προταθεί για το Όσκαρ Καλύτερης Ταινίας;

transpositions.why: Conventional Greek transliteration of the director's name.
Established Greek rendering of the award category.

substitution_note: No filmography or award referent is changed.

guide_gaps.why: Natural and established Greek name for the category.

reference_problems: The list is outdated: «Killers of the Flower Moon» was also nominated for Best Picture, bringing the number of Scorsese-directed nominees to ten as of the 2024 ceremony.
"Raging Bill" is a misspelling of the film title «Raging Bull».
Calling «The Departed» Scorsese's first Best Picture win is misleading: Best Picture is awarded to the credited producers, while Scorsese personally won Best Director.
The claim that «Goodfellas» gave Scorsese his third Best Director nomination is incorrect; it was his second, after «Raging Bull».
translator_notes: The prompt intentionally includes no cutoff year, matching the source; answers should therefore be current at generation time.

transpositions.why: Established Greek title of William Faulkner's novel.

substitution_note: The work is unchanged; its established Greek title is used.
reference_problems: The answer's broad statement that the family loses its religious faith over roughly thirty years oversimplifies the characters' differing relationships to religion.
